This round fixes every finding below before anything merges. 5c2's sweep will call this walk on paths it builds, so the walk must be right first.

The branch is story-430-s5c1-sweep-record, checked out in this worktree at round 1's head b9792375f (base bdf0e1ef8; four commits: 1fdd07a66 store v6, d9cf2c8f8 the walk, 7d4a325fb and b9792375f test fixes). When you are done, the branch is b9792375f plus your commits. Do not rebase, squash, amend or merge main: the controller restacks. Where a choice is left open below, implement the option marked recommended, keep it small, and say which you took in your notes.

READ FIRST:
- docs/decisions/0104-shared-local-hardware-sets-a-deadline-floor-and-the-host-sweeps-its-seat-trees.md, rulings 5, 7, 8 and 9 (as amended on this branch);
- the controller's 5c rulings on #430, https://github.com/feedback-loop-ai/brokkr/issues/430#issuecomment-6858698779;

THE JOURNAL RULE (operator and peer, 2026-11-13). Main is queue storage v5, and this branch makes it v6. A brokkr built from this tree migrates any journal it opens for writing, and the lanes' pinned engines cannot read a migrated journal.
- Never run a brokkr built from this tree against a journal outside a test's own temporary directory: not ~/source/feedback-loop-ai/the-forge/.forge/forge.db, and not this worktree's .forge/forge.db.
- **`brokkr doctor` counts.** Its database line opens the journal read-write and migrates it (crates/brokkr-cli/src/doctor/paths.rs, `report_database`, "Deliberately read-write"). Run it only with `--db` under a temporary directory.
- `brokkr compile` opens no journal.

THE FINDINGS TO FIX (round 1's review; each is a test case, reproduced by the reviewer):
1. **HIGH, security: the walk follows a link at the root when the root is spelled with a trailing separator or a final `.` or `..`.**
   - `statat` and `openat` receive the whole root path, and `O_NOFOLLOW` protects only a final component that is the link itself. POSIX resolves `<link>/` and `<link>/..` through the link.
   - **The case:** planted `<t>/target/kept` and the symlink `<t>/link -> target`.
     - `tree::remove_tree(Path::new("<t>/link/"))` unsealed and entered `target`, removed `target/kept`, and returned `Err(Io NotADirectory)`.
     - `remove_tree(Path::new("<t>/link/.."))` opened `<t>` and removed everything under it.
   - **Expected:** the same refusal the plain `<t>/link` root gets (`tree::tests::a_link_at_the_root_is_refused_and_its_target_stands`), with nothing removed.
   - **Recommended fix:**
     - the walk opens the root's parent as a directory, then opens the root by its final name with `O_NOFOLLOW | O_DIRECTORY` (and `statat` with `AT_SYMLINK_NOFOLLOW`) from that parent's descriptor;
     - a root whose final component is empty (a trailing separator), `.` or `..`, or that has no parent, is refused by name before anything opens.
     - Normalising the spelling instead is the alternative; name it as an ASK if you take it.
   - **Tests:** `<link>/`, `<link>/.`, `<link>/..`, `<dir>/.` and `<dir>/..` are each refused. The link's target and the parent's contents stand, with modes and contents pinned. A plain root is still removed.
2. **HIGH, a security smell: the run start's kept line carries a path that never passes `safe`.**
   - `Kept::Unremovable` wraps `TreeError`, whose `Display` is `removing <path>: <cause>`, and `Reaped::lines_with` (hands/session.rs:267) passes only the tree's own path through `safe`.
   - **The case:** a reaping root named `evil\n\x1b[31mname` (mode 0500), holding one dead owner's unheld `brokkr-hands-exec-<pid>-<uuid>` tree. The line carries the newline and the ESC.
   - **Expected:** no control byte reaches any line. A path below the root can be a file name a seat wrote inside the dead tree.
   - **Recommended fix:** the kept reason prints the cause alone, never a path, and the tree's path is the one `safe` already prints. Then check every line the reaper or the walk produces that names a path: each one goes through `safe`.
   - **Tests:** hostile names at the root and below it, on a kept tree and on a removed tree; no line holds a control byte.
3. **MEDIUM: the kept line's words changed while the commit says "byte for byte unchanged".** With item 2's fix, the line reads exactly as before this slice: `hands: kept <tree>: it cannot be removed: <cause>`. The session test pins that exact string, not one built from `why`'s own `Display`.
4. **MEDIUM: the count cannot read the trees the removal handles.**
   - `count_tree` never makes a directory owner-writable, so a nested directory at mode 0000 or 0200 makes `openat` fail. That is exactly what overlayfs leaves in a hands tree (the `sealed_overlay_work` fixture).
   - `list_reapable_in` drops a tree whose count fails, silently. So the reaper's listing, and 5c2's `--dry-run`, omit the normal hands shape.
   - **Recommended fix:**
     - the count never changes a mode, because a listing writes nothing;
     - a directory it cannot read makes the count a lower bound that names the first unreadable path;
     - a tree whose count fails is listed with that failure, never dropped.
     - Name the listing's words as an ASK.
   - **Tests:** a tree with `overlay/0/work/work` at mode 0000 holding a file. The listing names the tree, its lower bound and the unreadable path, and the removal still removes it and counts it whole.
5. **MEDIUM, exact coverage:** hands/session.rs:342's `if let Ok(Some(bytes)) = tree::count_tree(&tree)` has its second branch untaken, and :357's `Ok(None) => {}` has no hits. Item 4 changes both. Every new arm gets a test, including a tree that vanishes between the probe and the removal.
6. **LOW: `record_tree_sweep(kind, tree_seq: Option<i64>, …)`** lets a caller write the two invalid pairs, Scratch with no row and Hands with one, and they come back as a raw SQLite error. Recommended: the kind carries its row (`Swept::Scratch(seq) | Swept::Hands`), so neither is representable.
7. **LOW: `descend` drops a mid-listing readdir error** (`Dir::read_from(dir)?.flatten()`). Removal still fails closed, but names the wrong cause, and the count undercounts as `Ok`. Recommended: a readdir error is the walk's error for that directory, and item 4's lower bound for the count.
8. **LOW, tidy-ups:**
   - test_support.rs: `seat_tree_store` was inserted between `plant_run`'s doc comment and `plant_run`. Put `plant_run`'s doc back on it, and give `seat_tree_store` its own.
   - seat_tree/sweep.rs's module doc says a hands row "names neither", but R2 makes `generation` NOT NULL for hands rows too. Say what the code does.
   - Decision 0104's edits outside ruling 8 (the queue order, slice 5c's Files line, the price line) carry the house `*Amended, 2026-11-13 (controller, #430):*` marker, as ruling 8's own amendment does.

9. **brokkr-store lib.rs takes no net line from this branch.** Main reached its 800-line ceiling with #1078 (9933c0028, `StoreError::AfterTerminal`), and the controller restacks this branch onto it. Round 1 added two re-export lines to lib.rs. Recommended: reach those items through their module's path, or one `pub use` in that module, so lib.rs on this branch is back at its base length of 785. This realm is a Rust workspace. Production code is Rust under `crates/`; the
Rust-only architecture is recorded by decision 0009. Semantic changes carry a
decision document with status `proposed` because only the operator accepts one.
Intake seats read `README.md` and decisions 0004 and 0005 before framing a
commission, along with the code and history it touches.

The frozen v1 contracts under `contracts/`, the production table at
`policy/phase-machine.json`, and `reference/` (its schemas included) are
read-only.
A contract change lands as a new version file beside the old one, never as an
edit. The evaluator corpus under `fixtures/` is also frozen and is never
regenerated, only versioned.

Tests are part of every change. Extend the suite that proves the code, run
`cargo test --workspace`, compile `recipes/self`, and leave formatting, clippy,
and the exact-coverage gate clean before reporting success.

Commit completed work with `git` using the repository's message style. Never
push.

The supported hosts are Linux and macOS (decision 0063); WSL2 is Linux. Write
no Windows-conditional code, test or evidence.

## Architecture

Decision 0071 rules how code here is shaped. Build to it, and cite its ruling
numbers in what you judge. Where a gate named below holds a rule, the gate is
the authority, and a finding it would catch is the gate's.

- **Pure core (ruling 1).** `brokkr-core` and `brokkr-view` do no I/O and read
  no clock, environment or randomness. They run no process. Pass `now`, paths
  and environment in as arguments. Effects live in the crates above core and
  view, and are journaled.
- **Enums and data, not traits (ruling 2).** A closed set is an enum matched
  exhaustively, with no wildcard arm that decides behaviour. Anything an
  operator extends is data under `adapters/`, `agents/`, `recipes/` or
  `realms.json`, validated and digested. Add a trait only for a seam whose
  contract spans several operations that must stay consistent with one
  another, reached across a process or service boundary, and name that seam
  in its doc comment. `ProducerTransport` is the one such trait today. A test
  double alone does not make a seam: a single substitutable function is a
  closure seam (`*_with`, `*_in`), which is how the house inverts a
  dependency otherwise.
- **Typed at the edge (ruling 3).** Parse wire, file and harness data once
  into a type, with `serde` and `deny_unknown_fields` where the contract is
  closed. `serde_json::Value` never goes past the edge, into state, or back
  out by string key. Never put `format!("{:?}")` in anything digested or
  journaled. A doubly-optional field or a string vocabulary is a missing enum.
- **Small functions (ruling 4).** New and changed functions stay within 100
  lines, nesting depth 5 and 7 parameters. Cyclomatic complexity follows
  the operator's 2026-09-26 ruling: a function may reach the higher of 15
  and its baseline, so a new function stays within 15, an existing one may
  change freely up to 15, and one already over 15 may only shrink.
  Production files stay within 800 lines and test files within 2,000, and a
  file already over may not grow. Add no new `jscpd` clone in production
  code, test code or data. `quality/` holds the measured baseline. Today's
  offenders carry `#[allow(clippy::…)]`, and #337 converts them to
  `#[expect(clippy::…, reason = "…")]`. Add a suppression only by a ruling,
  and remove it when you fix the function. A new suppression is
  `#[expect(…, reason)]`, never `#[allow]`.
- **Once (ruling 5).** Every fact has one home. A repeated vocabulary, skeleton
  or helper becomes one function or one table. An agent is defined once under
  `agents/`, and seats hire it by reference. A recipe that differs from another
  by a model, a seat or an entry is an `extends` overlay, never a copy. The
  agent library does not yet accept `extends`, and #360 builds it. Until then,
  a variation of an agent lives at the seat that hires it, overridden in a
  recipe overlay. It is never a second agent file that restates the first. A
  copy that must exist, such as a script a bundle pins, is held to its source
  by a test.
- **Nothing unused (ruling 6).** Add no alias, agent, contract version, flag or
  `pub` item without a consumer, and prefer `pub(crate)`. A deprecation names
  the release that removes it.
- **One derivation (ruling 7).** A fact shown on two surfaces is derived once
  in `brokkr-view`. The CLI, the TUI and `ui.html` only paint it. The engine
  never admits anything by a display-crate function.
- **Typed errors (ruling 8).** Return a `thiserror` enum whose `Display` keeps
  the operator's text. Tests match variants and pin each module's text once.
  Add no new `Result<_, String>`.
